items.title: Feat(server): narrow the type of 'meta' when runtime meta value injected

labels.name: ❄️  icebox
labels.description: features / PRs that might be pick up in the future and can be handy to keep track of

items.body:
## 🎯 Changes

Feat(server): narrow the type of 'meta' when runtime meta value injected

Currently tRPC middlewares always assume that the type of `opts.meta`
is `Meta | undefined` even when a procedure injects metadata using
`.meta()` or `defaultMeta` is provided to `initTRPC().create()`.

This commit modifies the behavior so that whenever either `procedure.meta()`
or `defaultMeta` is provided, the type of Meta is narrowed in downstream
handlers.

The `RootConfig` created in `initTRPC` is now changed
from `Meta` to `Partial<Meta>`, since this facilitates removing the type:

`_meta: TConfig['_meta'] | undefined`

from the definition of `MiddlewareFunction` (this is needed so that middlewares
aren't always stuck assuming `opts.meta` is a union of `Meta` and `undefined`.

Note: this would have the potential to break users' typechecks if they are doing sth
like:

`if (opts.meta && !opts.meta.foo) { throw new Error("bang!"); }`

because with the changed types, `opts.meta` is Partial<Meta>. To combat this
I changed the definition of `MiddlewareFunction` to `Meta | undefined` ONLY when `meta`
has not been injected by a procedure or by `defaultMeta`, which should preserve
backwards compatibility, as without runtime injection, the runtime value of Meta
will be `undefined`.

## ✅ Checklist

- [x] I have followed the steps listed in the [Contributing guide](https://github.com/trpc/trpc/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [ ] If necessary, I have added documentation related to the changes made.
- [x] I have added or updated the tests related to the changes made.

items.title: Different types of `middlewareMarker`
items.body:
Hello,

We have two separate folder for backend and frontend in our repo (no workspace setup) as they are compiled in their respective directories.

In an attempt to introduce `trpc` I stumbled upon an issue that we have two copies of `@trpc/server` package - both in server's and in client's `node_modules`.
The problem is that when I import `AppRouter` type from the server to client - I get a type mismatch of the `middlewareMarker` which is a symbol created in [middlewares.ts](https://github.com/trpc/trpc/blob/4c91e920529daa4f7c1a88cbc7b0db8a5ed405ce/packages/server/src/internals/middlewares.ts#L4).
It seems like I have two symbols that are by definition different.

Is it intended to be so?
Do I have to migrate to common `node_modules` (via workspaces) or there is a way around it?

The code:
```ts
// backend/index.ts
import * as trpc from "trpc/server";

const router = trpc.router();
export type AppRouter = typeof router;
```

```ts
// frontend/index.ts
import {createReactQueryHooks} from "@trpc/react";
import type { AppRouter } from "../backend/index";

export const trpc = createReactQueryHooks<AppRouter>();
```

The error:
```ts
(property) BaseHandlerOptions<AnyRouter<any>, e.Request<ParamsDictionary, any, any, QueryString.ParsedQs, Record<string, any>>>.router: AnyRouter<any>
Type 'Router<Context, Context, {}, Record<"path", Procedure<Context, Context, {}, undefined, undefined, BlockView, unknown, BlockView>>, Record<...> & ... 37 more ... & Record<...>, Record<...>, DefaultErrorShape>' is not assignable to type 'AnyRouter<any>'.
  The types of '_def.middlewares' are incompatible between these types.
    Type 'MiddlewareFunction<Context, Context, {}>[]' is not assignable to type 'MiddlewareFunction<any, any, any>[]'.
      Type 'MiddlewareFunction<Context, Context, {}>' is not assignable to type 'MiddlewareFunction<any, any, any>'.
        Types of parameters 'opts' and 'opts' are incompatible.
          Type '{ ctx: any; type: ProcedureType; path: string; rawInput: unknown; meta?: any; next: { (): Promise<MiddlewareResult<any>>; <T>(opts: { ctx: T; }): Promise<MiddlewareResult<T>>; }; }' is not assignable to type '{ ctx: Context; type: ProcedureType; path: string; rawInput: unknown; meta?: {} | undefined; next: { (): Promise<MiddlewareResult<Context>>; <T>(opts: { ...; }): Promise<...>; }; }'.
            The types returned by 'next()' are incompatible between these types.
              Type 'Promise<MiddlewareResult<any>>' is not assignable to type 'Promise<MiddlewareResult<Context>>'.
                Type 'MiddlewareResult<any>' is not assignable to type 'MiddlewareResult<Context>'.
                  Type 'MiddlewareOKResult<any>' is not assignable to type 'MiddlewareResult<Context>'.
                    Type 'MiddlewareOKResult<any>' is not assignable to type 'MiddlewareOKResult<Context>'.
                      Types of property 'marker' are incompatible.
                        Type 'typeof import("/.../backend/node_modules/@trpc/server/dist/declarations/src/internals/middlewares").middlewareMarker' is not assignable to type 'typeof import("/.../frontend/node_modules/@trpc/server/dist/declarations/src/internals/middlewares").middlewareMarker'.ts(2322)
BaseHandlerOptions.d.ts(11, 5): The expected type comes from property 'router' which is declared here on type 'NodeHTTPHandlerOptions<AnyRouter<any>, Request<ParamsDictionary, any, any, ParsedQs, Record<string, any>>, Response<any, Record<string, any>>>'
```

items.title: Middleware: swap context

labels.name: 🧙🏻  typescript wizardry
labels.description: if you want a typescript-challenge, look at these

items.body:
From #818 

@KATT I created a new PR because I made a lot of (type-level) changes.

- Added TInputContext to Router and Procedure
- Tests to make sure context-swapping works and doesn't have unexpected side-effects
- Removed swapContext method for now - can be added later, but the use-case is supported via `return next({ ctx: ... })`
- Replaced `MiddlewareFunctionKeepContext` and `MiddlewareFunctionSwapContext` with a single `MiddlewareFunction` type with an overloaded `next` input
- Made `next({ ctx: ... })` a function which can pass anything to `ctx`. The type passed is inferred as the `TContext` for the middleware's return value - this gets the `expectTypeOf` test added in the previous PR working
- Removed a bunch of ` = any` in type args. It was hard to keep track of what needed to be changed when defaults were used. I don't think any were internal so I've left them like that, but worth taking a look
- Added a swap-context example to the docs

Notes for the future:

- The types in `procedure.ts` are a bit loose. It's internal, so that's ok as long as it's covered by tests, but I think the crux is that it uses a `middlewares` array. I haven't tried this at all, but I think we could get more type safety by requiring that a procedure has exactly one middleware, and adding some helpers which compose middlewares. That way we can properly keep track of input and output contexts, instead of procedures having a list of unknown -> unknown middlewares.
- Having `ProcedureWithInput` and `ProcedureWithoutInput` made this a bit harder than it feels like it should be. Maybe Procedure instances could always have inputs, where for convenience you can add queries/mutations/subscriptions to a router without, but the "input" defaults to `() => undefined` (which is a valid `ProcedureInputParserCustomValidatorEsque`, I believe)
- When classes/interfaces start having loads of generics like here, something I've tried before is to have a single generic with properties, so you can do something like `class Router<T extends TRouterOptions>{ ... }`. Then to get the context you do `T['context']`, to get queries it'd be `T['queries']`. This can make it easier to write helper functions and refactor things without having to duplicate the ever-growing `<TInputContext, TContext, TQueries, TMutations, TSubscriptions, TGodKnowsWhatElse>` typearg lists, or fall back on potentially dangerous `any` defaults.

items.title: [RFC] Add middleware `next()`-fn
items.body:
Middlewares will now have to call a `next()` function that you **have to** call.

### Example

> A middleware that measures the time of procedures

```ts
.middleware(async ({ ctx, path, next }) => {
  const start = Date.now()
  await next()
  const end = Date.now()
  console.log({path, took: end - start})
})
```
---

@mmkal @delaneyj - you've both championed this. I really don't like my implementation of the recursive async/await spaghetti, I wrote it in like 5 minutes, but the tests pass and it seems to work. You're both [added as contributors](https://github.com/trpc/trpc/invitations) so you can update the branch directly, would be great if one of you could clean up my implementation.

---

### Todos

- [x] First draft
- [x] Add tests
- [x] Make a prettier implementation
- [x] Update docs
- [x] Update examples

---
Closes #564  #586 #564
